title: Business Office Accounting Note: Applying Payments, Monthly Payment Plans and Refunding Credit Balances (Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program)
content:
**Accounting rule.** Charges on a Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program checkout are paid by the accepted payment methods and are applied to the checkout's oldest open charge first. Charges totalling at least the payment plan threshold may be paid in the plan's number of equal monthly payments, the last carrying any remaining cents. A credit balance is refunded by district check within the refund period of calendar days, and a refund is issued only on a checkout in status returned.

## How each part reads

**Applying a payment.** A payment is applied within the checkout it is made on, to the oldest open charge first. The balance a household owes on a checkout rises with usage, late, cleaning, repair and replacement charges and with refunds disbursed, and falls with payments and credits.

**Monthly payments.** The plan is available when the charges on the checkout total at least the threshold. The total is divided into the plan's number of equal monthly payments; any cents left over by the division are carried by the last payment. Paying in monthly payments is available to the family, not required of it.

**Refund of a credit balance.** A credit balance on a checkout is refunded by district check within the refund period of calendar days after the checkout closes. The refund is issued only when the system record shows that checkout in status returned; a checkout in any other status is not refunded. The status is read on the checkout that holds the credit balance.

| Status of the checkout holding the credit balance | Refund issued |
|---|---|
| returned | yes, by district check within the refund period |
| checked out | no |
| in repair | no |
| overdue | no |
| lost | no |

## Worked examples on hypothetical figures

Hypothetical threshold 150.00 and a plan of 4 monthly payments, chosen only for illustration.

1. Charges on one checkout total 230.05. The total is at least the threshold. Divided into 4 equal payments the first three are 57.51 each and the last carries the remaining cents, 57.52; together they make 230.05.
2. Charges total exactly 150.00. A total equal to the threshold is at least the threshold, so the plan is available.
3. A checkout has a usage fee posted first and a late fee posted later, both unpaid, and a payment of 30.00 is made. The payment is applied to the usage fee first, as the oldest open charge.
4. A checkout closed in status returned carries a credit balance of 25.00. The 25.00 is refunded by district check within the refund period.
